entry.title: Sage S2.1 Flash Technical Report
entry.summary:
We introduce Sage S1.5 Flash, a 320-billion-parameter general-purpose mixture-of-experts model designed to reason over scientific evidence and act in interactive environments. Sage Sci-Perception uses dedicated encoders for molecular graphs and biological sequences and represents spectra as ordered patches of measurements. Modality-specific projectors map these representations into the input space of a shared backbone, which processes them alongside text and images.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #combinatorics #agents

entry.title: Doom GPU Flame Graphs
entry.summary:
Imagine halving the resource costs of AI and what that could mean for the planet and the industry -- based on extreme estimates such savings could reduce the total US power usage by over 10% by 2030 1 . At Intel we've been creating a new analyzer tool to help reduce AI costs called AI Flame Graphs : a visualization that shows an AI accelerator or GPU hardware profile along with the full software stack, based on my CPU flame graphs . Our first version is available to customers in the Intel Tiber AI Cloud as a preview for the Intel Data Center GPU Max Series (previously called Ponte Vecchio).

Source: Brendan Gregg (Systems Performance & eBPF) · Tags: #kernel-os #performance #compilers #combinatorics

entry.title: Peak state transfer in trees and the cost of distance
entry.summary:
There is peak state transfer between vertices $u$ and $v$ in a graph $G$ if there exists a time $t$ for which $|(\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm i t M})_{u,v}|$ saturates the triangle inequality imposed by its spectral decomposition and $M$ is either the adjacency or Laplacian matrix. We show that peak state transfer at distance $d$ requires $\frac{d^3}{24}(1 + o(1))$ edges in the adjacency case, $Ω(d^2)$ edges in the Laplacian case, and that the leading coefficient in the former is tight. We find a family of graphs with Laplacian peak state transfer at distance $d$ and $Θ(d^5)$ edges, showing that peak state transfer is achievable in a polynomial graph size.

Source: arXiv Mathematics (NT, CO, AG, LO, AT, GR) · Tags: #number-theory #combinatorics #quantum-computing

entry.title: Complex Moments of the Derivative of the Riemann Zeta Function. We investigate the complex moments of the derivative of the Riemann zeta function through a random Euler product model.
entry.summary:
We investigate the complex moments of the derivative of the Riemann zeta function through a random Euler product model. For each fixed $σ>1/2$ and every $s\in\mathbb{C}$ with $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$, we show, under the Lindelöf hypothesis, that the $2s$-th moment of $|ζ'(σ+\mathrm{i}t)|$ over $t\in[1,T]$ converges, as $T\to\infty$, to the corresponding moment of the derivative of the random Euler product. We then establish, unconditionally, an asymptotic formula for the latter moment as $σ\downarrow 1/2$ throughout the half-plane $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$.

Source: arXiv Mathematics (NT, CO, AG, LO, AT, GR) · Tags: #number-theory #combinatorics #probability-stats #logic

entry.title: The Geometry of Zero Knowledge: Tight Masking and Efficient Multilinear Arguments
entry.summary:
Zero-knowledge proofs have become a fundamental tool for verifiable computation and privacy-preserving applications, driving growing interest in proof systems that are both succinct and efficient. In polynomial-based arguments, however, achieving zero knowledge introduces additional costs. Random masks must hide the evaluations and intermediate messages revealed during verification while preserving the underlying computation.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust #combinatorics

entry.title: Information-Theoretic Strong Traceable Secret Sharing Schemes. Traceable secret sharing complements traditional schemes by enabling the identification of parties who sell their shares.
entry.summary:
Traceable secret sharing complements traditional schemes by enabling the identification of parties who sell their shares. More precisely, a group of corrupted parties generates a reconstruction box $R$ that, given enough valid shares as input, reconstructs the secret. The goal is to trace $R$ back to at least one of the corrupted parties using only black-box access to it.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics

entry.title: One Fell Swoop: A Single-Trace Key-Recovery Attack on the Falcon Signing Algorithm
entry.summary:
Falcon, a lattice-based signature scheme selected for NIST post-quantum standardization, is notable for its compact signature size alongside a complex signing procedure involving extensive floating-point arithmetic. Prior side-channel attacks on Falcon signing, while demonstrating vulnerabilities, have consistently required a large number of power traces for successful key recovery, which limits their real-world practicality. This paper presents a new single-trace attack on the Falcon signing procedure.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #combinatorics
